verdict.rationale: Sprinto documents webhooks that receive external events and trigger ingestion workflows, and an AI Editor that builds and edits those workflows from natural-language prompts. That is an event-triggered, user-definable automation, but it is scoped to data ingestion. Beyond that there is only configurable AI risk auto-scoring with thresholds and generic monitoring alerts. missing for 10: a general-purpose rules engine (if-event-then-action across modules, e.g. auto-create tasks or notify), documented trigger/condition/action configuration, coverage of internal platform events beyond inbound webhooks, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: You can use webhooks to: Receive incoming payloads, Trigger ingestion workflows, Process external events
Sprinto’s AI Editor helps you create and modify ingestion workflows using natural language prompts.
You can configure: AI risk auto-scoring, Risk thresholds and scoring levels
Each webhook generates a unique endpoint URL that receives incoming requests from external services.
